inputs.abstract:
This submission formalizes deterministic algorithms for the
multicommodity flow–cut theorems of Leighton and Rao. The general statement
allows rational product demands, zero-weight transit vertices, and directed
or undirected capacities. One deterministic algorithm runs in time polynomial
in the binary encoding size of the rational input and returns a positive-demand
cut and an exact rational concurrent flow satisfying
$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(p)f$, where $p$ is the number of
positive-weight vertices. Directed, undirected, and uniform variants are
corollaries of this common guarantee. Arc-to-path conversion over real flows gives the
classical bound $\operatorname{sparsestCut}\le C\log_2(p)\operatorname{maxFlow}$.

The submission also includes the deterministic uniform short-path flow
construction of Theorem 18, with its simultaneous flow-value and path-length
guarantees. Algorithms use the exact LP solver of
[lax-109476](https://laxarchive.org/lax-109476/), the registered word RAM of
[lax-808846](https://laxarchive.org/lax-808846/) and the polynomial-time
predicate of [lax-759944](https://laxarchive.org/lax-759944/), measured in
binary rational input size and requiring exact encoded outputs.

concepts.title: Arc-to-path conversion for concurrent flows
concepts.description:
Every feasible concurrent arc flow can be replaced by a finite simple-path
flow of the same value. The conversion never increases the load on any
directed arc, so it preserves both separate directed capacities and shared
undirected capacities.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Capacities, vertex weights, and flows may be arbitrary nonnegative reals.
Cycles and diagonal commodities can be discarded. No positivity, symmetry,
or rationality assumption is needed for this representation theorem.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

/-!
---
title: Arc-to-path conversion for concurrent flows
type: lemma
---
Every feasible concurrent arc flow can be replaced by a finite simple-path
flow of the same value. The conversion never increases the load on any
directed arc, so it preserves both separate directed capacities and shared
undirected capacities.

# Formalization notes

Capacities, vertex weights, and flows may be arbitrary nonnegative reals.
Cycles and diagonal commodities can be discarded. No positivity, symmetry,
or rationality assumption is needed for this representation theorem.
-/

open scoped NNReal

namespace Lax455465.ArcToPath
open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

/-- Conservation and capacities in the arc formulation yield the public
simple-path formulation, with no increase in arc load. -/
axiom exists_path_flow {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (N : Network n)
    (π : VertexWeight n) (f : ℝ≥0) (F : ArcFlow n)
    (hF : IsArcConcurrentFlow kind N π f F) :
    ∃ P : PathFlow n, IsConcurrentFlow kind N π f P ∧
      ∀ u v, arcLoad P u v ≤ totalArcLoad F u v

end Lax455465.ArcToPath

statements.signature:
exists_path_flow : ∀ {n : Nat} (kind : Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind) (N : Lax455465.ProductNetwork.Network n)
  (π : Lax455465.ProductNetwork.VertexWeight n) (f : NNReal) (F : Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.ArcFlow n),
  Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.IsArcConcurrentFlow kind N π f F →
    Exists fun P =>
      And (Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.IsConcurrentFlow kind N π f P)
        (∀ (u v : Fin n),
          NNReal.instPartialOrder.le (Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.arcLoad P u v)
            (Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.totalArcLoad F u v))

concepts.title: Concurrent fractional flow
concepts.description:
A fractional flow can be represented by nonnegative commodity/arc amounts
or by nonnegative amounts on finitely many simple paths.
It is feasible when the total load on every edge is at most its capacity.
Undirected edges carry the sum of the loads in both directions; directed arcs
carry only forward load. A concurrent flow of value $f$ meets $f$ times
every commodity's demand simultaneously. The maximum concurrent flow is the
supremum of feasible values.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The ordinary algorithm uses arc amounts with exact supply and conservation,
so its certificate has polynomially many coordinates. The short-path
algorithm uses explicit path records to certify the lengths.

A path is its ordered vertex list. Positive flow is supported only on lists
with at least two vertices and no repeated vertex. Its commodity is determined
by its endpoints, rather than stored separately. Requiring at least the stated
demand allows excess flow; deleting excess gives the usual equality formulation.
Cycles are unnecessary for fractional routing and can be deleted.

For undirected product demand, each ordered pair receives $f\pi(u)\pi(v)/2$;
for directed product demand it receives $f\pi(u)\pi(v)$. Only distinct
endpoints impose demands. An absent edge has zero capacity, so feasibility
prevents a positive-flow path from using it. There are finitely many simple
paths on `Fin n`; with at least two positive-weight vertices, feasible values
form a nonempty bounded set and the supremum is attained.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.ProductNetwork
import Mathlib.Data.Finsupp.Defs
import Mathlib.Data.List.Count

/-!
---
title: Concurrent fractional flow
type: definition
---
A fractional flow can be represented by nonnegative commodity/arc amounts
or by nonnegative amounts on finitely many simple paths.
It is feasible when the total load on every edge is at most its capacity.
Undirected edges carry the sum of the loads in both directions; directed arcs
carry only forward load. A concurrent flow of value $f$ meets $f$ times
every commodity's demand simultaneously. The maximum concurrent flow is the
supremum of feasible values.

# Formalization notes

The ordinary algorithm uses arc amounts with exact supply and conservation,
so its certificate has polynomially many coordinates. The short-path
algorithm uses explicit path records to certify the lengths.

A path is its ordered vertex list. Positive flow is supported only on lists
with at least two vertices and no repeated vertex. Its commodity is determined
by its endpoints, rather than stored separately. Requiring at least the stated
demand allows excess flow; deleting excess gives the usual equality formulation.
Cycles are unnecessary for fractional routing and can be deleted.

For undirected product demand, each ordered pair receives $f\pi(u)\pi(v)/2$;
for directed product demand it receives $f\pi(u)\pi(v)$. Only distinct
endpoints impose demands. An absent edge has zero capacity, so feasibility
prevents a positive-flow path from using it. There are finitely many simple
paths on `Fin n`; with at least two positive-weight vertices, feasible values
form a nonempty bounded set and the supremum is attained.
-/

open scoped BigOperators NNReal

namespace Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

open Lax455465.ProductNetwork

/-- A finite assignment of nonnegative flow amounts to vertex lists. -/
abbrev PathFlow (n : ℕ) := List (Fin n) →₀ ℝ≥0

/-- Every path carrying positive flow is simple and has distinct endpoints. -/
def IsPathFlow {n : ℕ} (F : PathFlow n) : Prop :=
  ∀ P ∈ F.support, 2 ≤ P.length ∧ P.Nodup

/-- The forward load on an arc, counting its occurrences on each path. -/
noncomputable def arcLoad {n : ℕ} (F : PathFlow n) (u v : Fin n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  ∑ P ∈ F.support, F P * ((P.zip P.tail).count (u, v) : ℝ≥0)

/-- The capacity consumed by a path flow in the chosen edge model. -/
noncomputable def edgeLoad {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (F : PathFlow n)
    (u v : Fin n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  match kind with
  | .undirected => arcLoad F u v + arcLoad F v u
  | .directed => arcLoad F u v

/-- The amount routed from one endpoint to another. -/
noncomputable def routed {n : ℕ} (F : PathFlow n) (s t : Fin n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  ∑ P ∈ F.support,
    if P.head? = some s ∧ P.getLast? = some t then F P else 0

/-- The demand assigned to an ordered pair of distinct endpoints. -/
noncomputable def pairDemand {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (π : VertexWeight n)
    (s t : Fin n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  match kind with
  | .undirected => π s * π t / 2
  | .directed => π s * π t

/-- A simple-path flow respects capacities and meets the specified common
fraction of every demand. -/
def IsConcurrentFlow {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (N : Network n)
    (π : VertexWeight n) (f : ℝ≥0) (F : PathFlow n) : Prop :=
  IsPathFlow F ∧
    (∀ u v, edgeLoad kind F u v ≤ N.capacity u v) ∧
      ∀ s t, s ≠ t → f * pairDemand kind π s t ≤ routed F s t

/-- The largest feasible concurrent-flow value, expressed as a supremum. -/
noncomputable def maxFlow {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (N : Network n)
    (π : VertexWeight n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  sSup {f | ∃ F : PathFlow n, IsConcurrentFlow kind N π f F}

/-- An arc flow records a nonnegative amount for each commodity and arc. -/
abbrev ArcFlow (n : ℕ) := Fin n → Fin n → Fin n → Fin n → ℝ≥0

/-- Aggregate forward capacity consumption in the edge formulation. -/
def totalArcLoad {n : ℕ} (F : ArcFlow n) (u v : Fin n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  ∑ s, ∑ t, F s t u v

/-- Shared or separate capacities in the edge formulation. -/
def totalEdgeLoad {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (F : ArcFlow n) (u v : Fin n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  match kind with
  | .undirected => totalArcLoad F u v + totalArcLoad F v u
  | .directed => totalArcLoad F u v

/-- Net required supply at a vertex for one commodity; diagonal commodities
have zero supply at every vertex. -/
noncomputable def requiredSupply {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (π : VertexWeight n)
    (f : ℝ≥0) (s t u : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  if s = t then 0 else
    (if u = s then (f * pairDemand kind π s t : ℝ≥0) else 0) -
    (if u = t then (f * pairDemand kind π s t : ℝ≥0) else 0)

/-- Capacity and exact commodity conservation in the polynomial-size arc formulation. -/
def IsArcConcurrentFlow {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (N : Network n)
    (π : VertexWeight n) (f : ℝ≥0) (F : ArcFlow n) : Prop :=
  (∀ u v, totalEdgeLoad kind F u v ≤ N.capacity u v) ∧
  ∀ s t u, (∑ v, (F s t u v : ℝ)) - (∑ v, (F s t v u : ℝ)) =
    requiredSupply kind π f s t u

end Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

concepts.title: Exact flow–cut output certificates
concepts.description:
The output contains both a cut and a rational concurrent flow. For a product
instance with $p$ positive-weight vertices, the cut has positive demand, the
flow is feasible, and their values satisfy
$$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(p)\,f.$$
The same output witnesses both sides of the algorithmic flow–cut guarantee.
A zero-capacity cut and the zero flow are valid when the instance has no
positive concurrent flow.

sections.title: Formalization notes

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.RationalEncoding

/-!
---
title: Exact flow–cut output certificates
type: definition
---
The output contains both a cut and a rational concurrent flow. For a product
instance with $p$ positive-weight vertices, the cut has positive demand, the
flow is feasible, and their values satisfy
$$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(p)\,f.$$
The same output witnesses both sides of the algorithmic flow–cut guarantee.
A zero-capacity cut and the zero flow are valid when the instance has no
positive concurrent flow.

# Formalization notes

The output starts with the length-$n$ cut membership word, followed by the
existing rational arc-flow encoding. Validity is checked against the input;
an output annotation about its approximation ratio is never trusted.
-/

open scoped NNReal

namespace Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate

open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow Lax455465.RationalEncoding

/-- The cut and rational path flow returned by a flow–cut algorithm. -/
structure Certificate (n : ℕ) where
  /-- One shore of the cut. -/
  cut : Finset (Fin n)
  /-- A concurrent flow with an explicitly claimed value. -/
  flow : ArcCertificate n

/-- The exact output contains the cut followed by the flow certificate. -/
def encodeCertificate {n : ℕ} (certificate : Certificate n) : List ℕ :=
  encodeCut certificate.cut ++ encodeArcs certificate.flow

/-- The joint guarantee for directed and undirected product demands. -/
def IsValid {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (I : RationalInstance n) (C : ℝ)
    (certificate : Certificate n) : Prop :=
  AdmissibleCut I.weights certificate.cut ∧
  IsArcConcurrentFlow kind I.network I.weights
    (certificate.flow.value : ℝ≥0) certificate.flow.flow ∧
  (ratioCost I.network I.weights certificate.cut : ℝ) ≤
    C * logFactor (supportCount I.weights) * (certificate.flow.value : ℝ)

end Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate

concepts.title: Classical product multicommodity flow–cut bound
concepts.description:
For one universal constant $C>0$, every rational product-demand instance
with $p\ge2$ positive-weight vertices satisfies
$$\operatorname{sparsestCut}(G,\pi)
  \le C\log_2(p)\,\operatorname{maxFlow}(G,\pi).$$
The statement covers directed arcs with separate capacities and symmetric
undirected edges with shared capacities. Uniform demand is the all-one
specialization.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The maximum flow is the supremum over the real-valued simple-path flows
defined in `ConcurrentFlow`. This corollary uses the joint certificate
returned by the deterministic RAM algorithm and the public arc-to-path
conversion, connecting the algorithmic guarantee to the classical values.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.RamProductFlowCut
import Lax455465.ArcToPath

/-!
---
title: Classical product multicommodity flow–cut bound
type: lemma
---
For one universal constant $C>0$, every rational product-demand instance
with $p\ge2$ positive-weight vertices satisfies
$$\operatorname{sparsestCut}(G,\pi)
  \le C\log_2(p)\,\operatorname{maxFlow}(G,\pi).$$
The statement covers directed arcs with separate capacities and symmetric
undirected edges with shared capacities. Uniform demand is the all-one
specialization.

# Formalization notes

The maximum flow is the supremum over the real-valued simple-path flows
defined in `ConcurrentFlow`. This corollary uses the joint certificate
returned by the deterministic RAM algorithm and the public arc-to-path
conversion, connecting the algorithmic guarantee to the classical values.
-/

namespace Lax455465.ProductFlowCut
open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow Lax455465.RationalEncoding

/-- The classical flow–cut inequality follows from the constructive certificate. -/
axiom exists_flow_cut_bound :
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ (kind : EdgeKind) (n : ℕ) (I : RationalInstance n),
      (kind = .undirected → I.network.IsUndirected) →
      2 ≤ supportCount I.weights →
      (sparsestCut I.network I.weights : ℝ) ≤
        C * logFactor (supportCount I.weights) * (maxFlow kind I.network I.weights : ℝ)

end Lax455465.ProductFlowCut

statements.signature:
exists_flow_cut_bound : Exists fun C =>
  And (Real.instLT.lt 0 C)
    (∀ (kind : Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind) (n : Nat) (I : Lax455465.RationalEncoding.RationalInstance n),
      (Eq kind Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind.undirected → I.network.IsUndirected) →
        instLENat.le 2 (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.supportCount I.weights) →
          Real.instLE.le (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.sparsestCut I.network I.weights).toReal
            (instHMul.hMul
              (instHMul.hMul C (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.logFactor (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.supportCount I.weights)))
              (Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.maxFlow kind I.network I.weights).toReal))
statements.doc: The classical flow–cut inequality follows from the constructive certificate.

concepts.title: Product multicommodity networks and sparsest cuts
concepts.description:
A product multicommodity network has nonnegative edge capacities and a
nonnegative weight $\pi(v)$ at each vertex. In an undirected network, the
demand between distinct vertices $u,v$ is $\pi(u)\pi(v)$, shared equally
between the two directions. In a directed network, the demand from $u$ to $v$
is $\pi(u)\pi(v)$ in each direction separately. Uniform demands are the case
$\pi\equiv1$.

The ratio cost of a cut $(S,\overline S)$ is
$$\frac{C(S,\overline S)}{\pi(S)\pi(\overline S)}.$$
Its numerator counts each undirected crossing edge once, or only arcs leaving
$S$ in the directed case. The sparsest-cut value is the infimum of these
ratios over cuts of positive demand. Write $p$ for the number of vertices
of positive weight.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Vertices are `Fin n`. A capacity matrix represents parallel edges by their
total capacity and absent edges by zero; loops are excluded. An undirected
network has a symmetric capacity matrix. The same cut formula applies in
both cases. Cuts of zero demand are excluded, including empty cuts. When
$p\ge2$, the set of admissible cuts is finite and nonempty, so its infimum
is a minimum. The theorems impose this hypothesis explicitly.

The logarithmic factor is $\log_2 p$, as in the paper. Stating product
bounds in terms of $p$ also handles the two-terminal case, where the
paper's shorthand $\log k$ vanishes because $k=\binom p2=1$.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Powerset
import Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic

/-!
---
title: Product multicommodity networks and sparsest cuts
type: definition
---
A product multicommodity network has nonnegative edge capacities and a
nonnegative weight $\pi(v)$ at each vertex. In an undirected network, the
demand between distinct vertices $u,v$ is $\pi(u)\pi(v)$, shared equally
between the two directions. In a directed network, the demand from $u$ to $v$
is $\pi(u)\pi(v)$ in each direction separately. Uniform demands are the case
$\pi\equiv1$.

The ratio cost of a cut $(S,\overline S)$ is
$$\frac{C(S,\overline S)}{\pi(S)\pi(\overline S)}.$$
Its numerator counts each undirected crossing edge once, or only arcs leaving
$S$ in the directed case. The sparsest-cut value is the infimum of these
ratios over cuts of positive demand. Write $p$ for the number of vertices
of positive weight.

# Formalization notes

Vertices are `Fin n`. A capacity matrix represents parallel edges by their
total capacity and absent edges by zero; loops are excluded. An undirected
network has a symmetric capacity matrix. The same cut formula applies in
both cases. Cuts of zero demand are excluded, including empty cuts. When
$p\ge2$, the set of admissible cuts is finite and nonempty, so its infimum
is a minimum. The theorems impose this hypothesis explicitly.

The logarithmic factor is $\log_2 p$, as in the paper. Stating product
bounds in terms of $p$ also handles the two-terminal case, where the
paper's shorthand $\log k$ vanishes because $k=\binom p2=1$.
-/

open scoped BigOperators NNReal

namespace Lax455465.ProductNetwork

/-- Whether capacities are shared by both directions of an edge or belong
to individual directed arcs. -/
inductive EdgeKind
  /-- One capacity shared by both directions of an undirected edge. -/
  | undirected
  /-- A separate capacity for each directed arc. -/
  | directed
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A finite loopless network with nonnegative capacities. -/
structure Network (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The capacity of an edge or arc, with zero denoting absence. -/
  capacity : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ≥0
  /-- Loops are absent. -/
  loopless : ∀ v, capacity v v = 0

/-- An undirected network has the same capacity in both directions. -/
def Network.IsUndirected {n : ℕ} (N : Network n) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v, N.capacity u v = N.capacity v u

/-- The nonnegative weights whose products specify the demands. -/
abbrev VertexWeight (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ≥0

/-- The number of vertices with positive weight. -/
noncomputable def supportCount {n : ℕ} (π : VertexWeight n) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun v => 0 < π v).card

/-- The total vertex weight in a set. -/
def mass {n : ℕ} (π : VertexWeight n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ≥0 :=
  ∑ v ∈ S, π v

/-- A cut separates positive total weight on both sides. -/
def AdmissibleCut {n : ℕ} (π : VertexWeight n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  0 < mass π S ∧ 0 < mass π Sᶜ

/-- The capacity leaving a cut; symmetric capacities count an undirected
edge exactly once. -/
def cutCapacity {n : ℕ} (N : Network n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ≥0 :=
  ∑ u ∈ S, ∑ v ∈ Sᶜ, N.capacity u v

/-- The ratio of cut capacity to separated product demand. -/
noncomputable def ratioCost {n : ℕ} (N : Network n) (π : VertexWeight n)
    (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℝ≥0 :=
  cutCapacity N S / (mass π S * mass π Sᶜ)

/-- The least ratio cost of a cut with positive demand. -/
noncomputable def sparsestCut {n : ℕ} (N : Network n) (π : VertexWeight n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  sInf {r | ∃ S : Finset (Fin n), AdmissibleCut π S ∧ ratioCost N π S = r}

/-- The all-one vertex weights defining uniform demand. -/
def uniformWeight (n : ℕ) : VertexWeight n := fun _ => 1

/-- The paper's base-two logarithm. -/
noncomputable def logFactor (p : ℕ) : ℝ := Real.log (p : ℝ) / Real.log 2

end Lax455465.ProductNetwork

concepts.title: Deterministic directed product flow–cut algorithm
concepts.description:
A deterministic polynomial-time word RAM returns a cut and a rational
concurrent flow satisfying
$$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(p)\,f.$$
Both certificates concern the same rational product-demand instance.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This specializes the general product flow–cut algorithm to directed
capacities and demands, retaining its program, exact output, and binary-size
RAM bound. Undirected capacities are symmetric and shared between directions;
directed cuts count outgoing arcs and directed capacities may be asymmetric.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate

/-!
---
title: Deterministic directed product flow–cut algorithm
type: lemma
---
A deterministic polynomial-time word RAM returns a cut and a rational
concurrent flow satisfying
$$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(p)\,f.$$
Both certificates concern the same rational product-demand instance.

# Formalization notes

This specializes the general product flow–cut algorithm to directed
capacities and demands, retaining its program, exact output, and binary-size
RAM bound. Undirected capacities are symmetric and shared between directions;
directed cuts count outgoing arcs and directed capacities may be asymmetric.
-/

namespace Lax455465.RamDirectedSparsestCut

open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.RationalEncoding Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate
open Lax759944.RamPolytime

/-- The directed product specialization returns the joint certificate. -/
axiom exists_polynomial_time_sparse_cut :
  ∃ (solve : List ℕ → List ℕ) (C : ℝ), RamPolytime solve ∧ 0 < C ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (I : RationalInstance n), 2 ≤ supportCount I.weights →
      ∃ certificate : Certificate n,
        solve (encodeInput .directed I) = encodeCertificate certificate ∧
        IsValid .directed I C certificate

end Lax455465.RamDirectedSparsestCut

statements.signature:
exists_polynomial_time_sparse_cut : Exists fun solve =>
  Exists fun C =>
    And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime solve)
      (And (Real.instLT.lt 0 C)
        (∀ (n : Nat) (I : Lax455465.RationalEncoding.RationalInstance n),
          instLENat.le 2 (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.supportCount I.weights) →
            Exists fun certificate =>
              And
                (Eq (solve (Lax455465.RationalEncoding.encodeInput Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind.directed I))
                  (Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate.encodeCertificate certificate))
                (Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate.IsValid Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind.directed I C certificate)))
statements.doc: The directed product specialization returns the joint certificate.

concepts.title: Deterministic directed uniform flow–cut algorithm
concepts.description:
A deterministic polynomial-time word RAM returns a cut and a rational
uniform concurrent flow satisfying
$$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(n)\,f$$
on every rational directed $n$-vertex instance with $n\ge2$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
All input weights equal one. The proof specializes the directed product
algorithm; every vertex has positive weight, so $p=n$. Its program, exact
output, and registered RAM polynomial-time guarantee are retained.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate

/-!
---
title: Deterministic directed uniform flow–cut algorithm
type: lemma
---
A deterministic polynomial-time word RAM returns a cut and a rational
uniform concurrent flow satisfying
$$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(n)\,f$$
on every rational directed $n$-vertex instance with $n\ge2$.

# Formalization notes

All input weights equal one. The proof specializes the directed product
algorithm; every vertex has positive weight, so $p=n$. Its program, exact
output, and registered RAM polynomial-time guarantee are retained.
-/

open scoped NNReal

namespace Lax455465.RamDirectedUniformFlowCut

open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow
open Lax455465.RationalEncoding Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate Lax759944.RamPolytime

/-- The uniform directed specialization of the product algorithm. -/
axiom exists_polynomial_time_flow_cut :
  ∃ (solve : List ℕ → List ℕ) (C : ℝ), RamPolytime solve ∧ 0 < C ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (I : RationalInstance n), (∀ v, I.weight v = 1) → 2 ≤ n →
      ∃ certificate : Certificate n,
        solve (encodeInput .directed I) = encodeCertificate certificate ∧
        AdmissibleCut I.weights certificate.cut ∧
        IsArcConcurrentFlow .directed I.network I.weights
          (certificate.flow.value : ℝ≥0) certificate.flow.flow ∧
        (ratioCost I.network I.weights certificate.cut : ℝ) ≤
          C * logFactor n * (certificate.flow.value : ℝ)

end Lax455465.RamDirectedUniformFlowCut

statements.signature:
exists_polynomial_time_flow_cut : Exists fun solve =>
  Exists fun C =>
    And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime solve)
      (And (Real.instLT.lt 0 C)
        (∀ (n : Nat) (I : Lax455465.RationalEncoding.RationalInstance n),
          (∀ (v : Fin n), Eq (I.weight v) 1) →
            instLENat.le 2 n →
              Exists fun certificate =>
                And
                  (Eq (solve (Lax455465.RationalEncoding.encodeInput Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind.directed I))
                    (Lax455465.FlowCutCertificate.encodeCertificate certificate))
                  (And (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.AdmissibleCut I.weights certificate.cut)
                    (And
                      (Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.IsArcConcurrentFlow Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind.directed I.network
                        I.weights certificate.flow.value.cast certificate.flow.flow)
                      (Real.instLE.le (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.ratioCost I.network I.weights certificate.cut).toReal
                        (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul C (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.logFactor n))
                          certificate.flow.value.cast))))))

concepts.title: Deterministic polynomial-time product flow–cut algorithm
concepts.description:
One deterministic polynomial-time word-RAM algorithm returns a rational
concurrent flow and a positive-demand cut for every rational product-demand
instance with $p\ge2$ positive-weight vertices. Their values satisfy
$$\operatorname{ratio}(S)\le C\log_2(p)\,f$$
for one universal constant $C>0$. The input may have directed arcs with
asymmetric capacities, or undirected edges with shared capacities.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This is the constructive form of Theorems 7 and 17 of Leighton and Rao
(1999). Zero-weight transit vertices and arbitrary rational capacities and
weights are allowed. Uniform instances and the two edge models are
specializations of this single statement. The edge model is supplied in the
input encoding; its symmetry hypothesis applies to undirected instances.

The algorithm returns the exact joint certificate. The registered
`RamPolytime` predicate certifies a single deterministic program, measured
in binary input size, at every sufficiently large word length. Neither the
LP solution nor the rounding step is an assumed computational oracle.

concepts.title: Polynomial-time RAM construction of a uniform short-path flow
concepts.description:
There is a polynomial-time word-RAM algorithm and universal constants $A,B>0$
such that, on every rational undirected uniform instance with $n\ge2$ and
positive sparsest-cut value $\mathcal S$, it returns a rational fractional
flow certificate meeting a common fraction $f$ of all demands, where
$$\mathcal S\le A\log_2(n)f,$$
and every path carrying flow has length at most
$$\frac{B C_{\max}\log_2(n)}{n\mathcal S}.$$

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
This states the algorithmic assertion accompanying Theorem 18 of Leighton
and Rao (1999). The same decoded certificate must satisfy capacities, every
commodity demand, the flow-value bound, and the path-length bound. Its exact
rational output is produced by a program certified by the registered RAM
polynomial-time predicate. All-one weights are required in the input encoding.

import Lax455465.RationalEncoding
import Lax455465.ShortPathFlow

/-!
---
title: Polynomial-time RAM construction of a uniform short-path flow
type: theorem
---
There is a polynomial-time word-RAM algorithm and universal constants $A,B>0$
such that, on every rational undirected uniform instance with $n\ge2$ and
positive sparsest-cut value $\mathcal S$, it returns a rational fractional
flow certificate meeting a common fraction $f$ of all demands, where
$$\mathcal S\le A\log_2(n)f,$$
and every path carrying flow has length at most
$$\frac{B C_{\max}\log_2(n)}{n\mathcal S}.$$

# Formalization notes

This states the algorithmic assertion accompanying Theorem 18 of Leighton
and Rao (1999). The same decoded certificate must satisfy capacities, every
commodity demand, the flow-value bound, and the path-length bound. Its exact
rational output is produced by a program certified by the registered RAM
polynomial-time predicate. All-one weights are required in the input encoding.
-/

open scoped NNReal

namespace Lax455465.RamUniformShortPathFlow

open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow
open Lax455465.ShortPathFlow Lax455465.RationalEncoding Lax759944.RamPolytime

/-- A polynomial-time RAM constructs a feasible uniform flow with the
value and path-length guarantees of Theorem 18. -/
axiom exists_polynomial_time_short_path_flow :
  ∃ (solve : List ℕ → List ℕ) (A B : ℝ),
    RamPolytime solve ∧ 0 < A ∧ 0 < B ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (I : RationalInstance n),
        I.network.IsUndirected → (∀ v, I.weight v = 1) → 2 ≤ n →
          0 < sparsestCut I.network (uniformWeight n) →
            ∃ certificate : FlowCertificate n,
              solve (encodeInput .undirected I) = encodeFlow certificate ∧
              IsConcurrentFlow .undirected I.network (uniformWeight n)
                (certificate.value : ℝ≥0) certificate.flow ∧
              (sparsestCut I.network (uniformWeight n) : ℝ) ≤
                A * logFactor n * (certificate.value : ℝ) ∧
              HasPathLengthAtMost certificate.flow
                (B * (maxIncidentCapacity I.network : ℝ) * logFactor n /
                  ((n : ℝ) * (sparsestCut I.network (uniformWeight n) : ℝ)))

end Lax455465.RamUniformShortPathFlow

  Exists fun A =>
    Exists fun B =>
      And (Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime solve)
        (And (Real.instLT.lt 0 A)
          (And (Real.instLT.lt 0 B)
            (∀ (n : Nat) (I : Lax455465.RationalEncoding.RationalInstance n),
              I.network.IsUndirected →
                (∀ (v : Fin n), Eq (I.weight v) 1) →
                  instLENat.le 2 n →
                    NNReal.instPartialOrder.lt 0
                        (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.sparsestCut I.network (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.uniformWeight n)) →
                      Exists fun certificate =>
                        And
                          (Eq
                            (solve
                              (Lax455465.RationalEncoding.encodeInput Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind.undirected I))
                            (Lax455465.RationalEncoding.encodeFlow certificate))
                          (And
                            (Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow.IsConcurrentFlow Lax455465.ProductNetwork.EdgeKind.undirected
                              I.network (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.uniformWeight n) certificate.value.cast
                              certificate.flow)
                            (And
                              (Real.instLE.le
                                (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.sparsestCut I.network
                                    (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.uniformWeight n)).toReal
                                (instHMul.hMul (instHMul.hMul A (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.logFactor n))
                                  certificate.value.cast))
                              (Lax455465.ShortPathFlow.HasPathLengthAtMost certificate.flow
                                (instHDiv.hDiv
                                  (instHMul.hMul
                                    (instHMul.hMul B (Lax455465.ShortPathFlow.maxIncidentCapacity I.network).toReal)
                                    (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.logFactor n))
                                  (instHMul.hMul n.cast
                                    (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.sparsestCut I.network
                                        (Lax455465.ProductNetwork.uniformWeight n)).toReal))))))))

concepts.title: Rational flow instances and certificates
concepts.description:
Finite algorithms receive nonnegative rational capacities and vertex weights.
Each rational is encoded by its reduced numerator and positive denominator.
An instance contains its edge model, number of vertices, vertex weights in
vertex order, and full capacity matrix in row order. A cut is encoded by
its length-$n$ membership word. An ordinary flow certificate contains its claimed value and the $n^4$
commodity/arc amounts. A short-path certificate instead contains its value
and a list of paths with rational flow amounts.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The dense encoding covers arbitrary rational capacities and weights, including
zero weights and absent edges. The first entry distinguishes directed from
undirected instances. Cut entries are exactly zero or one. A flow certificate
starts with the numerator and denominator of its value and the number of
path records; each record contains its vertex-count, vertex list, numerator,
and denominator. Repeated path records contribute their summed amount.

Algorithms use `Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime` directly. It quantifies
one actual program, polynomial word and instruction bounds in the binary
input size, and exact execution at every sufficiently large word length on
Lax808846's registered word RAM. The physical tape has the length prefix
specified by that predicate. No new machine or abstract cost oracle is used.
The algorithm's function is total; its output on malformed inputs is unconstrained.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow
import Lax759944.RamPolytime
import Mathlib.Data.NNRat.Lemmas

/-!
---
title: Rational flow instances and certificates
type: definition
---
Finite algorithms receive nonnegative rational capacities and vertex weights.
Each rational is encoded by its reduced numerator and positive denominator.
An instance contains its edge model, number of vertices, vertex weights in
vertex order, and full capacity matrix in row order. A cut is encoded by
its length-$n$ membership word. An ordinary flow certificate contains its claimed value and the $n^4$
commodity/arc amounts. A short-path certificate instead contains its value
and a list of paths with rational flow amounts.

# Formalization notes

The dense encoding covers arbitrary rational capacities and weights, including
zero weights and absent edges. The first entry distinguishes directed from
undirected instances. Cut entries are exactly zero or one. A flow certificate
starts with the numerator and denominator of its value and the number of
path records; each record contains its vertex-count, vertex list, numerator,
and denominator. Repeated path records contribute their summed amount.

Algorithms use `Lax759944.RamPolytime.RamPolytime` directly. It quantifies
one actual program, polynomial word and instruction bounds in the binary
input size, and exact execution at every sufficiently large word length on
Lax808846's registered word RAM. The physical tape has the length prefix
specified by that predicate. No new machine or abstract cost oracle is used.
The algorithm's function is total; its output on malformed inputs is unconstrained.
-/

open scoped NNReal NNRat

namespace Lax455465.RationalEncoding

open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

/-- A product instance with nonnegative rational capacities and weights. -/
structure RationalInstance (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The rational capacity of each edge or directed arc. -/
  capacity : Fin n → Fin n → ℚ≥0
  /-- Loops have zero capacity. -/
  loopless : ∀ v, capacity v v = 0
  /-- The rational weights specifying product demands. -/
  weight : Fin n → ℚ≥0

/-- Interpret rational capacities as exact nonnegative real capacities. -/
def RationalInstance.network {n : ℕ} (I : RationalInstance n) : Network n where
  capacity u v := (I.capacity u v : ℝ≥0)
  loopless v := by simpa using congrArg (fun q : ℚ≥0 => (q : ℝ≥0)) (I.loopless v)

/-- Interpret rational vertex weights as exact nonnegative real weights. -/
def RationalInstance.weights {n : ℕ} (I : RationalInstance n) : VertexWeight n :=
  fun v => (I.weight v : ℝ≥0)

/-- Encode a nonnegative rational by its canonical numerator and denominator. -/
def encodeRational (q : ℚ≥0) : List ℕ := [q.num, q.den]

/-- Encode the edge model, order, weights, and row-major capacity matrix. -/
def encodeInput {n : ℕ} (kind : EdgeKind) (I : RationalInstance n) : List ℕ :=
  [match kind with | .undirected => 0 | .directed => 1, n] ++
    (List.ofFn I.weight).flatMap encodeRational ++
    (List.ofFn fun u => List.ofFn (I.capacity u)).flatten.flatMap encodeRational

/-- Encode a shore as its length-`n` membership word. -/
def encodeCut {n : ℕ} (S : Finset (Fin n)) : List ℕ :=
  List.ofFn fun v => if v ∈ S then 1 else 0

/-- A finite rational flow certificate, with its claimed concurrent value. -/
structure FlowCertificate (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The common fraction of demand claimed by the certificate. -/
  value : ℚ≥0
  /-- Paths and their flow amounts; duplicate records are added together. -/
  paths : List (List (Fin n) × ℚ≥0)

/-- The exact fractional path flow represented by a certificate. -/
noncomputable def FlowCertificate.flow {n : ℕ} (certificate : FlowCertificate n) :
    PathFlow n :=
  certificate.paths.foldl
    (fun F record => F + Finsupp.single record.1 (record.2 : ℝ≥0)) 0

/-- Encode a certificate's value and its length-prefixed rational path records. -/
def encodeFlow {n : ℕ} (certificate : FlowCertificate n) : List ℕ :=
  encodeRational certificate.value ++ [certificate.paths.length] ++
    certificate.paths.flatMap fun record =>
      [record.1.length] ++ record.1.map Fin.val ++ encodeRational record.2

/-- A polynomial-size rational arc-flow certificate for the ordinary theorem. -/
structure ArcCertificate (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The common demand fraction. -/
  value : ℚ≥0
  /-- The amount assigned to each commodity and directed arc. -/
  arcs : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n → Fin n → ℚ≥0

/-- Exact real interpretation of rational commodity/arc amounts. -/
def ArcCertificate.flow {n : ℕ} (certificate : ArcCertificate n) : ArcFlow n :=
  fun s t u v => (certificate.arcs s t u v : ℝ≥0)

/-- The value followed by all n⁴ arc coordinates in index order. -/
def encodeArcs {n : ℕ} (certificate : ArcCertificate n) : List ℕ :=
  encodeRational certificate.value ++
    (List.ofFn fun s => List.ofFn fun t => List.ofFn fun u => List.ofFn fun v =>
      encodeRational (certificate.arcs s t u v)).flatten.flatten.flatten.flatten

end Lax455465.RationalEncoding

concepts.title: Concurrent flow on short paths
concepts.description:
The length of a path is its number of edges. A fractional flow has path
length at most $L$ if every path carrying positive flow has at most $L$
edges. For an undirected network, $C_{\max}$ is the largest total capacity
incident to a single vertex.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Path lengths are integers, compared with a real bound. Only the support
of the fractional flow matters. Incident capacity sums the capacity matrix
along one row, counting each edge incident to the vertex once.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

/-!
---
title: Concurrent flow on short paths
type: definition
---
The length of a path is its number of edges. A fractional flow has path
length at most $L$ if every path carrying positive flow has at most $L$
edges. For an undirected network, $C_{\max}$ is the largest total capacity
incident to a single vertex.

# Formalization notes

Path lengths are integers, compared with a real bound. Only the support
of the fractional flow matters. Incident capacity sums the capacity matrix
along one row, counting each edge incident to the vertex once.
-/

open scoped BigOperators NNReal

namespace Lax455465.ShortPathFlow

open Lax455465.ProductNetwork Lax455465.ConcurrentFlow

/-- Every path carrying flow has at most `L` edges. -/
def HasPathLengthAtMost {n : ℕ} (F : PathFlow n) (L : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ P ∈ F.support, ((P.length - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ L

/-- The largest total capacity incident to one vertex. -/
noncomputable def maxIncidentCapacity {n : ℕ} (N : Network n) : ℝ≥0 :=
  sSup {r | ∃ v : Fin n, (∑ u : Fin n, N.capacity v u) = r}

end Lax455465.ShortPathFlow

proofs.description:
Extract simple positive paths by repeated bottleneck subtraction for each
off-diagonal commodity. Conservation supplies a path whenever residual supply
is positive, even if the residual contains cycles. Each subtraction either
finishes the supply or removes a positive arc, giving finite termination.
Adding the commodity path flows preserves capacities and the common value.

Specialize the general algorithm to directed input words. Asymmetric
capacities require no symmetry assumption.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
The implication conditioned on undirected mode has a false antecedent.
All certificate and execution guarantees are inherited directly.

proofs.description:
The directed uniform algorithm is the directed product algorithm on all-one
weights, with full unit demand for each distinct ordered pair.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Rewrite the demand-support cardinality to the input order in the directed
product certificate guarantee. The RAM program itself is retained.

proofs.description:
Specialize the general algorithm to undirected input words and symmetric
capacities. The program, resource bounds and joint output are unchanged.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Apply the general certificate guarantee with the undirected mode. The
symmetry implication is discharged by the input's symmetry hypothesis.

proofs.description: The undirected uniform algorithm is the product algorithm on all-one weights.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Every vertex belongs to the demand support, so its size is the input order.
Use the undirected product guarantee and rewrite its logarithmic factor.

proofs.description:
The deterministic algorithm supplies an admissible cut and a feasible arc
flow. Public arc-to-path conversion puts its value in the feasible set defining
`maxFlow`; the boundedness lemma makes that value at most the supremum. The
admissible cut bounds the infimum defining `sparsestCut`, yielding the classical
inequality with the algorithm's same universal approximation constant.

One fixed RAM program constructs the joint flow–cut certificate in both
edge models, with universal approximation constant 512.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Compile the complete valid-input pipeline: the registered exact LP solver,
rational directed distances, deterministic metric rounding, and certificate
output. A bounded interpreter computes the source word width and clock from
the actual binary input size. Its execution and polynomial resource proofs
apply to every input word. On valid networks its clock contains the complete
source execution, so it emits exactly the certified output. Compiler transfer
establishes the existing uniform word-RAM predicate at every sufficient host
word width.

proofs.description:
One fixed polynomial-time RAM program constructs the rational short-path
flow of Theorem 18, with universal constants 32768 and 8192.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
The program reads the source graph, computes the maximum incident capacity,
and invokes the registered exact LP solver on successive layered networks.
It implements the stopping test and extracts the selected primal solution
by deterministic positive-path traversal, bottleneck subtraction, and online
cycle erasure. Conservation and capacity invariants certify the actual emitted
records. A common denominator lattice bounds every residual word independently
of the number of updates. The complete execution has polynomial word and
instruction bounds; compiler simulation and a bounded interpreter establish
the registered uniform RAM predicate on every input.
